history.summary: One of the 52 Shakti Peethas, at the confluence of the Shankini and Dankini rivers in Dantewada. Legend holds that Sati's tooth (dant) fell here, which gave the town and the goddess their names. Sources conflict on the builders: most say the Chalukyas of the South or the Kakatiya kings of Warangal built it in the 14th century; one account credits King Annam Dev. The goddess is the Kuldevi of the erstwhile Bastar royal house and is revered by local tribal communities; her black-stone, six-armed idol is the focus of the 75-day Bastar Dussehra, when she is taken out in procession. The complex has four parts: Garbha Griha, Maha Mandap, Mukhya Mandap and Sabha Mandap, with a Garuda pillar at the entrance. NOTE: the 'Danteshwari temple Jagdalpur' with a white idol mentioned on Wikipedia is a separate shrine, not this one.

name: Danteshwari Temple
town_description: Dantewada is a town and the administrative headquarters of Dantewada district in the Bastar division of south Chhattisgarh, situated at the confluence of the Shankini and Dankini rivers. Its earlier names were Tarlapal and Dantawali, and the present name derives from Goddess Danteshwari, the town's presiding deity and one of the 52 Shakti Peethas. The district is part of the forested, iron-ore-rich Bastar region, famous for the Bailadila mines and the 75-day Bastar Dussehra festival.
